question.text: For an ordinary (non-PAN-exempt) individual mutual fund applicant, which of the following is the mandatory Proof of Identity (PoI) under the standard KYC framework?

answer.text: Latest utility bill with the applicant's name

explanation.text: The Logic: Workbook page 158 of NISM Series II-B (December 2025) makes PAN card with photograph the mandatory Proof of Identity for ordinary (non-PAN-exempt) individual mutual fund applicants. Alternate OVDs such as Aadhaar, Voter ID, and driving licence become relevant only in PAN-exempt or OVD contexts (pp.158-159). The Trap: Bank passbook, utility bill, and rent agreement are typically address-related documents, not the mandatory PoI for ordinary applicants. The audit flagged the original because the stem asked simply "what is accepted as PoI" and included Aadhaar / Voter ID / driving licence as options - in the PAN-exempt or OVD contexts those are also defensibly accepted, so the original had multiple supportable answers. Note: The original was ambiguous because pp.158-159 also permit alternate photo identification/OVDs in PAN-exempt and OVD contexts. The stem has been narrowed to "ordinary (non-PAN-exempt) individual applicant" and the OVD distractors have been replaced with address-type documents, leaving PAN card with photograph as the unique mandatory PoI.
